metadata.original_text: This time series records palladium USD t oz data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-02-03 to 2025-02-18. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A January 2025 report on the catalytic converter recycling market revealed a significant trend of US recyclers stockpiling converters. This strategic decision was a direct response to the low price environment for Platinum Group Metals (PGMs), as the average value of catalytic converters had dropped by more than half following the historic highs of 2021 and 2022. The practice of stockpiling, however, presents a considerable risk due to the record-breaking rates of catalytic converter theft. The report emphasized the critical choices recyclers faced regarding their inventory—whether to hold, sell, or process—amidst the prevailing market uncertainty. Market conditions, including a strong dollar, inflation, and global economic uncertainty, drew parallels to the volatile PGM market of the early 2000s. <2> Multiple financial analysts and institutions have released forecasts for the 2025 palladium market, indicating a general consensus of a weaker market due to factors like oversupply and decreasing demand, particularly from the automotive sector. Price predictions for palladium in 2025 are varied. The CPM Group anticipates prices will stay within the $900–$1,000 per ounce range. Heraeus Precious Metals offers a wider forecast of $800–$1,200 per ounce, suggesting potential volatility. In contrast, some projections are more bearish; for instance, Trading Economics forecasts a continued downtrend to approximately $775 in the first quarter of 2025. Other analysts present a mixed outlook, with ANZ Research predicting an increase to $1,080/oz, while Fitch Ratings expects the price to hold steady at $1,050. The transition to electric vehicles, which do not use palladium in their catalytic converters, is a significant factor influencing these long-term forecasts. The World Platinum Investment Council predicts the palladium market will shift to a surplus from 2025. <3> On December 10, 2024, Heraeus Precious Metals released its "Precious Forecast 2025," predicting a decline in demand for palladium from the automotive sector for the upcoming year. The report attributes this anticipated decrease to the growing market share of battery electric vehicles (EVs) at the expense of traditional internal combustion engine vehicles. The automotive industry is the largest consumer of palladium, using over 80% of the supply, primarily for catalytic converters. While overall new vehicle sales are expected to rise in 2025, Heraeus forecasts that the growth in EV market share will outpace this, leading to a slight fall in the sales of combustion engine cars and consequently, lower palladium demand. The increasing use of tri-metal catalysts, where platinum is substituted for palladium, has also been a contributing factor in curbing demand growth. <4> The United States proposed to its Group of Seven (G-7) allies that they consider imposing sanctions on Russian palladium and titanium. This suggestion, made around October 22, 2024, was met with skepticism regarding its likelihood of success, primarily due to Europe's significant reliance on these metals for key industries. Despite the low probability of implementation, the proposal renewed concerns within the automotive industry about potential supply chain disruptions, as palladium is a vital component in the manufacturing of car catalysts and computer chips. <5> In October 2024, the price of palladium surged significantly due to the U.S. administration's proposal of potential sanctions on Russian palladium exports. The proposal was discussed during a meeting of G-7 deputy finance ministers in Washington on October 22, 2024. This news sparked fears of a supply disruption, as Russia is the world's largest producer of palladium, accounting for approximately 40% of the global output. Following the announcement, palladium prices saw a dramatic increase, with some reports indicating a surge of over 7% to nearly 10% on October 24th. U.S. spot markets recorded a 7% increase for the month of October. The potential sanctions were part of the Biden administration's efforts to exert further economic pressure on Russia. While the U.S. floated the idea, convincing European allies was noted as a potential challenge due to their reliance on the metal. <6> The outlook indicated that the declining trend for palladium remained intact; Prices fell sharply in early August in response to weakness in the U.S. jobs market; The report forecasted that prices would likely linger between $880 and $980 for the remainder of the year <7> Economic data provider Trading Economics forecasted that palladium prices would decrease in the latter half of 2024. The forecast, published on August 29, 2024, estimated the metal would trade at $823.76 per ounce in the third quarter before declining to $798.78 per ounce in the final quarter of the year. This prediction was part of a broader analysis of the palladium market, which also included forecasts from other entities like ANZ Research and Fitch Ratings. <8> A retrospective report on the first half of 2024 detailed the price fluctuations of palladium during the second quarter. The price of palladium commenced the quarter on April 1st at approximately US$996.28. It subsequently reached a year-to-date high of US$1,098 on April 9th. Following this peak, the price experienced a decline, dropping below the US$900 mark at the beginning of June. The quarter concluded with a surge in price, ending at US$963.50 on June 28th. <9> A report analyzed the first half of 2024 regarding palladium price.; The palladium price ended the second quarter at US$963.50 on June 28.; The palladium price regressed to US$881 on July 29. <10> A review of the first half of 2024 confirmed significant price volatility for palladium. [1] The year began with the price at $1,096 per ounce. [1] It subsequently fell to a yearly low of $859.15 on February 9, before experiencing an upward momentum in March, alongside other precious metals. [1]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Palladium prices in the US surged to a year-to-date high, touching $1,650 per Troy ounce for the first time since February 2023 and marking a 79.9% year-to-date increase. The market rally has been driven by slowing electric vehicle adoption trends and ongoing concerns over Russian supply reliability. <2> Heraeus Precious Metals published its 2026 forecast, predicting that palladium will face a wider market surplus and trade within a range of $950 to $1,500 per ounce. The firm cited headwinds from declining automotive consumption of palladium as battery electric vehicles (BEVs) continue to gain market share globally. <3> On November 14, 2025, Palladium spot prices in New York plunged nearly 3% (2.98%), dropping $42.00 to $1,368.00 per ounce. This decline was part of a broader sell-off across the precious metals market. The significant downturn was primarily driven by aggressive profit-taking, a reduction in safe-haven demand, and hawkish signals from U.S. Federal Reserve officials that diminished earlier expectations for near-term interest rate cuts. <4> In the third quarter of 2025, attributable palladium production from the Stillwater mines in the United States saw a significant decrease of approximately 34% when compared to the same period in 2024. The primary reason for this decline was lower throughput, a direct result of the Stillwater West operations being placed on care and maintenance in September 2024. The production for the third quarter of 2025, ending on September 30, was reported to be 2,700 ounces of attributable palladium. <5> In a Reuters poll of 30 analysts and traders conducted in late October 2025, the median forecast for the price of palladium in 2026 was significantly increased to $1,262.50 an ounce, up from $1,100 in a previous poll. This upward revision was attributed to several factors: a strong price performance in 2025, ; constraints on mine supply; and uncertainty regarding potential new U.S. tariffs on critical mineral imports, particularly on palladium from major producer, Russia. <6> In its annual 'Precious Metals Investment Focus 2025/2026' report, published on October 25, 2025, leading precious metals consultancy Metals Focus presented a bearish outlook for palladium. The firm forecasts that the palladium market deficit will shrink from 566,000 ounces in 2024 to 367,000 ounces in 2025, and narrow further to 178,000 ounces in 2026. This is attributed to a projected decline in automotive demand of just over 1 percent in 2026, coupled with a 10 percent increase in secondary supply from recycling activities. Consequently, Metals Focus projects palladium prices will average $1,350 per ounce in the fourth quarter of 2025, before falling to an average of $1,150 by the fourth quarter of 2026. <7> Palladium prices surged in October 2025, climbing approximately 26% during the month to trade around $1,500 per ounce. The rally saw prices reach a peak of $1,655 on October 16th, the highest level in over two years, before pulling back. The significant price increase was part of a broader rally in precious metals and was attributed to several factors. Key drivers included expectations of interest rate cuts by the U.S. Federal Reserve, a less-hawkish monetary policy, and a weaker U.S. dollar. Tighter market supply, influenced by factors such as reduced mine output in South Africa, also contributed to the upward momentum. The Federal Reserve did enact a 25-basis-point rate cut at its meeting on October 29, 2025. <8> The Aberdeen Standard Physical Palladium Shares ETF (PALL) reached a new 52-week high of $148.49 on October 16, 2025. The increase was attributed to several factors, including rising US-China trade tensions, which led investors to view palladium as a safe-haven asset. Additionally, expectations of US interest rate cuts and a potential decline in the US dollar also contributed to the surge in palladium's price. <9> On July 30, 2025, an antidumping duty petition concerning imports of unwrought palladium from the Russian Federation was filed with the U.S. Department of Commerce. <10> A retrospective report on the first half of 2025 detailed a significant upward trend for palladium prices in the second quarter. Following tariff announcements in early April, the price dropped to a year-to-date low of US$866 on April 8. However, prices rebounded for the remainder of the quarter. The upward trend saw palladium break the US$1,000 mark at the end of May, reaching US$1,031 on May 21. The momentum continued into June, with the price reaching US$1,149 on June 26 before closing the quarter at $1,107.10 on June 30.

This upward movement was largely attributed to global supply concerns, particularly from major producers Russia and South Africa, which fueled risk-based premiums. However, this short-term rally occurred within a broader context of sustained long-term downward pressure on palladium prices. The primary factors contributing to this negative outlook are the expanding market share of battery electric vehicles (EVs), which do not use palladium in their exhaust systems, and the ongoing substitution of palladium with the less expensive platinum in the catalytic converters of gasoline-powered vehicles. Market forecasts for 2025 generally anticipate weaker fundamentals for palladium, with the potential for oversupply and decreasing demand from the automotive sector. While the growth of the EV market is a principal driver of this trend, a slower-than-expected EV adoption rate and a surprising increase in hybrid vehicle production in Q3 2025, which still utilize palladium, have provided some temporary support for demand. <7> On December 29, 2025, the CME Group raised initial and maintenance margin requirements for COMEX palladium futures, alongside gold, silver, and platinum. The margin hike forced traders to post additional collateral to maintain their positions, which amplified short-term selling pressure in the US market as leveraged participants were driven to trim their exposure. <8> On December 19, 2025, an intelligence memorandum titled 'The Palladium Paradox' was published, detailing an unprecedented market disconnect in the palladium sector. The report revealed that speculators in the US futures market had built their third consecutive all-time bearish extreme position—collectively betting approximately 50 tonnes on a price drop—despite the market experiencing 13 consecutive years of global physical supply deficits since 2012. <9> Palladium prices in the US surged to a year-to-date high, touching $1,650 per Troy ounce for the first time since February 2023 and marking a 79.9% year-to-date increase. The market rally has been driven by slowing electric vehicle adoption trends and ongoing concerns over Russian supply reliability.
